mkg.content.r1.excerpt: Breaks down the three most common selection mistakes for home storage in Germany - judging only by cell brand, only by cycle count, and ignoring inverter compatibility - each paired with one actionable test. Aimed at end users comparing quotes.
mkg.content.r2.excerpt: A 15-second vertical unboxing: full product shot in the first 3 seconds, one full charge-discharge cycle in the middle, and a price anchor plus purchase link at the end. Built for fast mobile-first discovery.
mkg.content.r3.excerpt: A quotation email for German dealers covering tiered discount thresholds, payment terms and freight basis, with a one-page quote attached. Written to be read directly by a purchasing lead.
mkg.content.r4.excerpt: Field data on capacity retention and temperature rise at 50C, with two lab comparison charts. Aimed at Middle East dealers and engineering customers - choose with evidence in hot climates.

A {{type}} draft built on the “{{script}}” framework from {{count}} materials:

With energy prices climbing across Europe, more households are looking for a safe, reliable backup power source. This piece follows a real need: it shows the core value of a balcony storage system — quick install, instant response, and App-based monitoring — through a real scenario plus a product demo, so the audience builds purchase trust and moves toward a conversion step via a limited-time offer and a free site survey.

Estimated reach: 120k · Target market: Germany · Suggested channels: TikTok, Instagram

intel.opp.energy.op1.name: Germany balcony storage kit opportunity
intel.opp.energy.op1.competition: The top three hold 64% of the market, yet their products cluster at 1–2 kWh. Nothing mature exists above 2.5 kWh, leaving a gap in the €700–1,000 band.
intel.opp.energy.op1.good1: Renters cannot install rooftop PV; a balcony kit is the only lawful alternative
intel.opp.energy.op1.good2: Germany exempted plug-and-play PV from approval from 2026, removing the installation barrier
intel.opp.energy.op1.good3: Electricity prices remain high; payback is about 3.2 years, a strong purchase driver
intel.opp.energy.op1.bad1: The grid-tie inverter needs VDE-AR-N 4105 certification — about 14 weeks
intel.opp.energy.op1.bad2: Load-bearing and waterproofing complaints make up 31% of negative reviews
intel.opp.energy.op1.bad3: Local installers dominate distribution, so reaching buyers directly is costly
intel.opp.energy.op1.brief: Enter the €749 band with a 2.5 kWh stackable module, a tool-free mounting bracket and an IP65 junction box — the first storage kit for renters.
intel.opp.energy.op1.feature: Stackable 2.5 kWh modules covering one night of base load
intel.opp.energy.op1.competitiveness: Tool-free mounting with pre-cleared VDE certification; rivals need 14 weeks to catch up
intel.opp.energy.op2.name: France outdoor portable power opportunity
intel.opp.energy.op2.competition: Jackery and Bluetti together hold 50%, mostly below 500 Wh. Above 1 kWh for outdoor use remains underserved.
intel.opp.energy.op2.good1: Camper and RV ownership grew 47% over three years, steadily lifting outdoor power demand
intel.opp.energy.op2.good2: French campsites permit powered pitches without extra approval
